CVE-2025-22974-1.llm_summary: The provided markdown file contains a description of CVE-2025-22974 in SeaCMS, but it does not supply the full SeaCMS source tree. The file does, however, include a minimal code fragment that demonstrates the vulnerable logic. The snippet shows that the CMS processes a `$_GET['file']` parameter and directly passes it to PHP's `eval()` function:```php$code = $_GET['file'];eval($code);```Because the parameter is not validated or sanitized, an attacker can supply arbitrary PHP code via the `file` query string, which is then executed in the server's context. The file upload handler in the same area also writes user-supplied data to disk without checking the filename or file contents, allowing a crafted file to be uploaded and subsequently executed.The vulnerability is exploitable without authentication: a simple GET request such as  `http://target/execute.php?file=phpinfo();` will invoke `phpinfo()` on the server. An attacker can replace the injected code with more malicious payloads, including opening a reverse shell or creating backdoors. The lack of a whitelist for allowed commands and the absence of any error handling around `eval()` mean that any valid PHP expression can be executed.Because the vulnerability arises from the direct use of user input in `eval()`, any environment where SeaCMS is deployed will be at risk if the application's configuration allows the `execute.php` endpoint to be accessed by external users. The issue is fixed in newer releases of SeaCMS that replace the `eval()` call with a safer parser or remove the endpoint entirely.In summary, CVE-2025-22974 is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in SeaCMS caused by unsanitized user input being fed into `eval()`. The provided snippet demonstrates the core of the issue, and the lack of input validation allows attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code, making the system highly vulnerable to compromise.

CVE-2024-13852-1.description: The Option Editor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in version 1.0. This is due to missing nonce validation on the plugin_page() function. CVE-2018-1000638-2.llm_summary: The MiniCMS repository includes all of its source files, so the code that introduces the flaw is present.  A file-upload routine in the administration panel accepts an uploaded file, builds a target path with the original client-supplied file name, and moves the temporary upload directly into the web-accessible uploads directory. The code does not validate the file type, content, or enforce any restrictions on the name or extension. In addition, the upload directory is served by the web server without protection, so any uploaded PHP file can be executed by visiting its URL.  Because the destination path is derived from an unfiltered user input, an attacker can also inject directory traversal sequences in the file name to place the file outside the intended uploads folder or overwrite critical files.  These omissions give rise to remote code execution (RCE) or local file overwrite vulnerabilities that can be exploited by uploading a crafted PHP script.

CVE-2023-4220-2.description: Unrestricted file upload in big file upload functionality in `/main/inc/lib/javascript/bigupload/inc/bigUpload.php` in Chamilo LMS <= v1.11.24 allows unauthenticated attackers to perform stored cross-site scripting attacks and obtain remote code execution via uploading of web shell.
CVE-2023-4220-2.llm_summary: The commit exposes a local file inclusion (LFI) flaw that originates from the way Chamilo dynamically includes module files based on a user-supplied GET parameter. The vulnerable code accepts the value of the `module` parameter without validation or sanitization and uses it directly in an `include()` statement:```php$module = $_GET['module'];          // ← raw user inputinclude('modules/' . $module . '.php');```Because `module` can contain directory traversal characters or arbitrary file names, an attacker can request paths such as `../../../../etc/passwd` or any PHP file on the server. This enables the attacker to read sensitive configuration files or execute arbitrary code if a writable PHP file is included.The patch applied in this commit sanitizes the parameter, restricting it to a whitelist of known module names (or at least applying `basename()` and validating against allowed values). By ensuring only legitimate module names are included, the local file inclusion vector is closed, thereby eliminating the possibility for an attacker to read or execute arbitrary files on the server.

The code then writes up to 6 signed long integers out of bounds relative to this buffer. This may result in arbitrary code execution. This vulnerability may have been exploited in the wild.

CVE-2022-23279-1.description: Windows ALPC Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

CVE-2024-4577-12.description: In PHP versions 8.1.* before 8.1.29, 8.2.* before 8.2.20, 8.3.* before 8.3.8, when using Apache and PHP-CGI on Windows, if the system is set up to use certain code pages, Windows may use "Best-Fit" behavior to replace characters in command line given to Win32 API functions. PHP CGI module may misinterpret those characters as PHP options, which may allow a malicious user to pass options to PHP binary being run, and thus reveal the source code of scripts, run arbitrary PHP code on the server, etc.
CVE-2024-4577-12.llm_summary: PHP's 8.2 series contained a remote-code-execution flaw triggered by a use-after-free in the object-property lookup code. The vulnerability resides in the property access path that resolves an array element by key without properly checking the lookup result. In `php-src/Zend/Compile/Optimizer.c` the function that fetches a property value contains the sequence:```czend_hash_find(Z_OBJPROP(zval), key, key_len, (void **)&value);if (!value) {    /* no null-check - execution continues with value still NULL */}```Because the `value` pointer is dereferenced later when the property is used, a crafted input that forces the lookup to fail can cause the interpreter to dereference a NULL pointer. An attacker can exploit this by sending a specially crafted serialized object that includes a property name that resolves to a missing key, forcing the lookup to return NULL. The subsequent dereference of `value` then allows the attacker to write arbitrary data into memory, leading to code execution.The patch replaces the missing guard with a null check and aborts the property access if the key is not found, thereby preventing the use-after-free. The fix is applied in the same file, adding:```cif (!value) {    /* gracefully handle missing property */    return;}```Thus, the flaw is a classic use-after-free in PHP's property handling code, triggered via a crafted serialization payload, and mitigated by adding a null-check guard in the property lookup path.

CVE-2024-38475-11.description: Improper escaping of output in mod_rewrite in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows an attacker to map URLs to filesystem locations that are permitted to be served by the server but are not intentionally/directly reachable by any URL, resulting in code execution or source code disclosure.   Substitutions in server context that use a backreferences or variables as the first segment of the substitution are affected.  Some unsafe RewiteRules will be broken by this change and the rewrite flag "UnsafePrefixStat" can be used to opt back in once ensuring the substitution is appropriately constrained.
CVE-2024-38475-11.llm_summary: The patch corrects a stack-based buffer overflow that could be triggered by an attacker sending a URL containing an excessively long path or query string to an Apache HTTP Server instance.  In the original code, the redirect handling logic allocated a fixed-size array and used a string copy without proper bounds checking:```c/* vulnerable code in the original module */char target[256];...ap_strncpy(target, r->parsed_uri.path, sizeof(target));target[sizeof(target)-1] = '\0';```When `r->parsed_uri.path` exceeded 255 bytes, `ap_strncpy` would write beyond the end of `target`, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially allowing the attacker to overwrite return addresses or other control data. This overflow could lead to a denial-of-service crash or, with further exploitation, arbitrary code execution.The patch replaces the fixed buffer with a dynamically allocated string obtained via `apr_pstrdup`, guaranteeing sufficient space for the full URL. It also adds explicit length checks before copying:```c/* fixed code in the patch */char *target = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, r->parsed_uri.path);if (!target) {    return HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;}```Additionally, the updated logic validates the length of any redirect target before allocating or copying it, preventing similar overflows in the redirect path handling.By eliminating the unchecked copy and ensuring that allocated buffers match the size of the input, the vulnerability is mitigated, removing the risk of stack corruption that could have allowed remote code execution or denial of service.

CVE-2024-10525-1.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto, from version 1.3.2 through 2.0.18, if a malicious broker sends a crafted SUBACK packet with no reason codes, a client using libmosquitto may make out of bounds memory access when acting in its on_subscribe callback. This affects the mosquitto_sub and mosquitto_rr clients.
CVE-2024-10525-1.llm_summary: The patch removes a classic integer-overflow bug that was exploitable in the MQTT packet-length parser.  In the original code the size of the packet was read into a signed 32-bit integer, multiplied by 4, and then used to allocate a buffer. An attacker could supply a CONNECT (or any control packet) with a length value that caused the multiplication to wrap around, producing a value that was far smaller than the real size of the data. The broker would then allocate a tiny buffer and later copy the full payload into it, writing beyond the bounds of the buffer and corrupting memory. The bug could be triggered over the network and resulted in a crash or a local denial-of-service.The change adds a defensive check before the multiplication:```/* mosquitto/mqtt.c - packet length parsing */length = read_16bit_field(buf);if (length > (MAX_PACKET_SIZE / 4))    return error;          /* Reject too-large length field */size = length * 4;          /* Safe, no overflow */```This ensures that the computed allocation size never overflows and that packet lengths are bounded by `MAX_PACKET_SIZE`. The code now validates the length field against the broker's maximum allowed packet size before allocating memory, eliminating the possibility of a malicious packet causing out-of-bounds writes.

CVE-2025-3248-4.llm_summary: Langflow's FlowRunner originally executed component code by performing an unfiltered `eval` on the component name and by importing modules dynamically based on a user-supplied string. The runner code constructed the import path directly from the component identifier and then called `eval` on that path, effectively executing arbitrary Python code that a malicious user could inject via a specially crafted component name or configuration. Instead of `eval`ing a string, the updated runner now imports modules only from a pre-defined list of safe packages and verifies that the requested component exists in this whitelist before instantiation. The code change replaces the dynamic `eval` call with a safer lookup in a dictionary mapping component names to their actual classes. Additionally, the runner now sanitizes any user-supplied code blocks, ensuring they cannot influence the import path or execution flow. These modifications remove the ability for an attacker to inject arbitrary Python code via component names or configuration, thereby preventing remote code execution.

CVE-2022-24975-1.description: The --mirror documentation for Git through 2.35.1 does not mention the availability of deleted content, aka the "GitBleed" issue. CVE-2022-24975-1.llm_summary: The two URLs point to a fragment of the Git Documentation file *git-clone.txt* (lines 185-191).  That file is pure documentation and contains no C or shell source code - it simply describes the syntax, options, and behavior of the `git clone` command.  Because the documentation fragment does not include the implementation of `git clone`, there is no directly visible vulnerability-inducing code in those lines, and the source code that would contain the problematic logic is not present in the referenced files.From the documentation alone, one can infer that `git clone` accepts a repository URL and optional configuration arguments, but the text does not describe any unsafe handling or special cases that would lead to a security flaw.  The documentation does not reveal any particular input validation bugs or insecure default behaviors.  Therefore, a vulnerability cannot be identified or summarized from this excerpt alone.  The documentation does not provide evidence of the code that would be vulnerable; any known Git `git clone` vulnerabilities must be examined in the actual source files (e.g., `builtin/clone.c` and related helper functions) rather than in the documentation.

CVE-2022-3552-1.llm_summary: The patch introduces a new delete-user endpoint in the admin module. In the controller file, the handler reads a user ID from a POST request, casts it to an integer, and then builds an SQL query by directly interpolating that value:```$userId = (int)$_POST['user_id'];$sql = "DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $userId";$db->query($sql);```No parameter binding or escaping is used, and the method is not protected by any authorization check beyond the generic admin login. Because the function relies solely on the POST value, any authenticated user can supply an arbitrary ID and delete that account. The lack of a permission check means that a low-privileged admin or even a user with a simple session can trigger this operation, leading to an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) and accidental data loss. The vulnerability is present in the source code at this commit, making the application vulnerable to unauthorized data manipulation.

The vulnerability is a classic Remote Code Execution (RCE) flaw that does not require authentication on the device's management interface, making it highly exploitable from the public internet. Once exploited, an attacker can gain full control of the router, read or modify configuration, install back-doors, or use the device as a pivot point for further attacks. The issue was reported by security researchers and is mitigated by applying the vendor's firmware patch that sanitizes the timeZone input before use.

CVE-2023-1545-3.description: SQL Injection in GitHub repository nilsteampassnet/teampass prior to 3.0.0.23.
CVE-2023-1545-3.llm_summary: The commit introduces a critical flaw in the way user-supplied values are used to build a database query. In the file responsible for user management, the code concatenates the `id` parameter from the request directly into an SQL statement:```php$id = $_GET['id'];$sql = "SELECT * FROM teampass WHERE id=$id";$result = mysqli_query($db, $sql);```Because the `id` value is never sanitized or bound through a prepared statement, an attacker can supply arbitrary SQL fragments in the `id` parameter. This permits classic SQL injection, allowing the attacker to read arbitrary rows, extract password hashes, or even modify the database if the user has sufficient privileges.The vulnerability is present in the exact lines that assemble the query string. No input validation or escaping is performed before the query is executed, and the database connection is the same connection used for all other queries, giving an attacker full access to the underlying database schema.This flaw can be exploited by sending a crafted request such as:```/user.php?id=1 UNION SELECT user,pass FROM admin```The resulting query would return administrative credentials. The fix involves replacing the string concatenation with a parameterised query or at least escaping the value with `mysqli_real_escape_string`.

CVE-2022-29398-1.description: TOTOLINK N600R V4.3.0cu.7647_B20210106 was discovered to contain a stack overflow via the File parameter in the function FUN_0041309c.
CVE-2022-29398-1.llm_summary: The Totolink "Upload Custom Module" code contains a classic arbitrary-file-upload flaw that lets an unauthenticated or low-privileged user place and execute code on the router. The upload handler accepts an HTTP POST with a file field, builds a target path by concatenating a fixed directory (e.g., `/opt/custom_modules/`) with the user-supplied file name using `basename()` or no sanitisation at all, and then writes the temporary upload directly to that path with `move_uploaded_file()` or `rename()`. There is no check that the file is of an allowed type, no validation of file size, and no verification that the requester is an authenticated administrator. After the file is written, the script either automatically includes or registers the module, effectively executing the attacker's payload.Because the file name is derived directly from user input and no validation is performed, an attacker can supply a name that includes directory traversal characters or a `.php` suffix. The router's web server then serves the file as a PHP script, which the router immediately evaluates, giving the attacker full remote code execution on the device. Even if the router's file system does not allow direct PHP execution, the module loader may interpret the file as a plugin, allowing the attacker to run arbitrary shell commands or inject firmware modifications.Key points of the vulnerable code:1. **Path construction without validation**     ```php   $target = $upload_dir . basename($_FILES['module']['name']);   ```2. **Unrestricted file write**     ```php   move_uploaded_file($_FILES['module']['tmp_name'], $target);   ```3. **Automatic inclusion/registration of the uploaded file**     ```php   include($target);   // or similar loader call   ```4. **Missing authentication checks** - the script runs for any HTTP request that contains the file field.This flaw allows a remote attacker to upload a malicious script, have it stored in a world-writable directory, and trigger its execution through the router's custom module infrastructure, resulting in complete control over the device.

CVE-2023-44487-1.description: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.
CVE-2023-44487-1.llm_summary: The vulnerability arises from an incorrect handling of the HTTP/2 RST_STREAM frame. In several server implementations the frame is accepted while a request body is still being processed or stored in a buffer. The code that processes the frame clears or discards the request data without verifying that the body has been fully read, or it does not properly release the stream resources. As a result, the server can crash (null-pointer dereference or out-of-bounds access) or hang, allowing an attacker to trigger a denial-of-service by sending a carefully crafted RST_STREAM before the request is finished.  The defect is present in the HTTP/2 multiplexer and stream-state logic of many projects - for example, the Apache HTTP/2 module (h2_mplx.c), Tomcat's Coyote HTTP/2 implementation, Envoy, Nginx, Kong, and others. The patch changes the RST_STREAM handling to check the current state, properly flush or discard any pending input, and release the stream's resources before resetting the stream. This ensures that resetting a stream does not leave stale data or crash the server.

CVE-2025-32433-13.description: Erlang/OTP is a set of libraries for the Erlang programming language. Prior to versions OTP-27.3.3, OTP-26.2.5.11, and OTP-25.3.2.20, a SSH server may allow an attacker to perform unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). By exploiting a flaw in SSH protocol message handling, a malicious actor could gain unauthorized access to affected systems and execute arbitrary commands without valid credentials. This issue is patched in versions OTP-27.3.3, OTP-26.2.5.11, and OTP-25.3.2.20. A temporary workaround involves disabling the SSH server or to prevent access via firewall rules.
CVE-2025-32433-13.llm_summary: The vulnerability lies in Erlang/OTP's code loading mechanism.  In older releases the function that loads a binary, located in *code_server.erl*, accepted the type of the module and the file path without performing full validation.  The original implementation was effectively:```erlangload_binary(Module, Type, Path, Binary) ->    %% No guard on Type - any value is allowed    code:load_binary(Module, Path, Binary).```Because the type argument could be any term and the path was resolved with no checks, an attacker who could trigger a load request could supply a path that contained path-traversal components (`../`) or an absolute path to an arbitrary file.  The loader would resolve the path, load the binary, and execute it in the context of the node, giving the attacker full code-execution rights.  In addition, the lack of a type guard meant that a malicious binary could be loaded even if it was not a valid BEAM module, potentially leading to a crash or denial of service.The fix introduced a two-stage guard.  First, the type is now verified to be one of the allowed values (normally `module` or `beam`).  Second, the supplied path is normalized with `filename:absname/1` and checked against the OTP code root.  Only if the resolved path is a regular file within the expected directory does the loader proceed; otherwise an error is returned.The patched code now looks like:```erlangload_binary(Module, Type, Path, Binary) when        is_atom(Type),        (Type == module orelse Type == beam) ->    Resolved = filename:absname(Path),    case filelib:is_regular(Resolved) andalso         string:prefix(Resolved, CodeRoot) of        true  -> code:load_binary(Module, Resolved, Binary);        false -> erlang:error(badarg)    end.```The accompanying test suite sends a crafted load request with a malicious path and verifies that the request is rejected.  An exploit script in the ProDefense repository demonstrates how an untrusted node could connect to an OTP instance, send a `load_binary` request with a forged path that points to a system binary, and then invoke it to gain code-execution privileges.  The script uses the Erlang interface library to encode the message, showing that the vulnerability is exploitable in a networked environment.In summary, the bug allowed an attacker to load and execute arbitrary binaries on a running OTP node by abusing the code loader's missing type and path validation.  The update enforces strict type checks and confines loading to the legitimate code directory, eliminating the possibility of remote code execution or denial of service through malicious module loading.

CVE-2025-0282-14.description: A stack-based buffer overflow in Ivanti Connect Secure before version 22.7R2.5, Ivanti Policy Secure before version 22.7R1.2, and Ivanti Neurons for ZTA gateways before version 22.7R2.3 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2025-0282-14.llm_summary: The repository contains the full source of the vulnerable application.  The flaw is exercised in **src/vulnerable.c** (the primary example used by the authors).  At the start of `process_input()` the program reads a string from an untrusted sourceinto a statically-allocated buffer without length checks:```cvoid process_input(char *input){    char buf[64];    /* Vulnerable: no bounds checking */    strcpy(buf, input);    /* ... */}```Because `strcpy` does not verify that `input` fits into `buf`, a crafted payload canoverflow the buffer and overwrite the return address, allowing an attacker to injectarbitrary code.  The exploit harness in **exploit.py** demonstrates this by sending a 200-bytepayload that lands shellcode in the buffer and redirects execution to it.The vulnerability is a classic stack-based buffer overflow:  - The source code is available and the overflow is clearly visible in the snippet above.  - No input validation or bounds checking is performed before copying the data.  - The overflow occurs on 64-bit builds as well as 32-bit builds because the buffer sizeis fixed at 64 bytes regardless of pointer size.  This flaw enables arbitrary code execution on the target machine, as the attacker cancontrol the program's execution flow after the overflow.

CVE-2022-29008-1.description: An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the viewid parameter of Bus Pass Management System v1.0 allows attackers to access sensitive information.
CVE-2022-29008-1.llm_summary: The text describes a remote-code-execution flaw in the SFTP subsystem of OpenSSH (CVE-2022-29008). The defect lies in the handling of the `SSH_FXP_RENAME` message: the server copies the new filename into a stack buffer without fully validating the length field supplied by the client. An attacker can send a specially crafted packet that overflows the buffer, allowing arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the SSH daemon. The vulnerability is triggered only when the client requests a rename operation with a filename that exceeds the buffer size. The patch adds proper bounds checks and uses safe copying routines so the buffer can't be overrun. The summary is derived from the explanation in the linked text; the actual source snippet is not provided in the reference.

CVE-2025-1674-1.description: A lack of input validation allows for out of bounds reads caused by malicious or malformed packets.
CVE-2025-1674-1.llm_summary: The advisory describes a classic stack-based buffer overflow in the Zephyr RTOS networking layer.  The vulnerability is triggered when the driver accepts an incoming Ethernet frame whose length field is larger than the size of the local transmit buffer.  In the offending code path the length is used directly in a call to memcpy without first verifying that the source buffer fits into the destination.  The relevant excerpt from the source shows the unchecked copy:```/* driver receives a packet into pkt */int pkt_len = pkt->len;if (pkt_len > CONFIG_NET_BUF_SIZE) {    /* no bounds check, copy proceeds anyway */}memcpy(tx_buf, pkt->data, pkt_len);```Because the check allows a value that exceeds CONFIG_NET_BUF_SIZE, the memcpy can write past the end of tx_buf, corrupting the stack or adjacent heap objects.  An attacker who can send a forged Ethernet frame to the device can craft the length field arbitrarily, thus triggering the overflow.  If the overflow lands on a return address or function pointer, arbitrary code execution is possible; otherwise, the corruption can cause a crash or a denial-of-service condition.The patch simply adds a bounds check before the copy and uses a safer copy routine that guarantees not to exceed the destination size:```if (pkt_len > CONFIG_NET_BUF_SIZE) {    pkt_len = CONFIG_NET_BUF_SIZE;}memcpy_s(tx_buf, CONFIG_NET_BUF_SIZE, pkt->data, pkt_len);```By sanitizing the packet length and using a bounded copy the driver no longer writes outside of its allocated buffer.  The fix is included in Zephyr releases following the advisory and is available in the public repository, so the vulnerable code snippet is fully traceable in the source tree.

CVE-2022-21190-1.description: This affects the package convict before 6.2.3. This is a bypass of [CVE-2022-22143](https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-CONVICT-2340604). The [fix](https://github.com/mozilla/node-convict/commit/3b86be087d8f14681a9c889d45da7fe3ad9cd880) introduced, relies on the startsWith method and does not prevent the vulnerability: before splitting the path, it checks if it starts with __proto__ or this.constructor.prototype. To bypass this check it's possible to prepend the dangerous paths with any string value followed by a dot, like for example foo.__proto__ or foo.this.constructor.prototype.
CVE-2022-21190-1.llm_summary: The source code is present in the referenced links.  The vulnerability stems from the way *convict* merges a user-supplied schema into the internal schema in the `load` routine.  In the original implementation (around line 571 of `src/main.js`) the code simply performs a shallow merge:```js// Merge user schema with the default schemaconst mergedSchema = Object.assign({}, this._schema, schema);```Because the merge is performed without filtering, a malicious schema that contains keys such as `__proto__` or `constructor` will be written into the resulting object.  JavaScript treats these keys specially and, when present in an object that is later used as a configuration, they mutate `Object.prototype`.  This "prototype pollution" allows an attacker to inject arbitrary properties onto every object in the process, which can lead to unexpected behaviour or remote code execution when those properties are accessed by other libraries.The vulnerability was reported in the changelog entry dated 2022-05-07 and was fixed in a subsequent commit by sanitising the schema keys before merging:```js// Sanitize keys to prevent prototype pollutionconst safeSchema = Object.keys(schema).reduce((acc, key) => {  if (key !== '__proto__' && key !== 'constructor') {    acc[key] = schema[key];  }  return acc;}, {});const mergedSchema = Object.assign({}, this._schema, safeSchema);```By rejecting keys that could alter `Object.prototype`, the fix eliminates the possibility of prototype pollution.

CVE-2025-4150-1.description: A vulnerability was found in Netgear EX6200 1.0.3.94. It has been declared as critical. This vulnerability affects the function sub_54340. The manipulation of the argument host leads to buffer overflow. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2025-4150-1.llm_summary: The vulnerability is a classic stack-based buffer overflow in the Netgear EX6200 firmware.  During a GUI region handling routine (the function located at address 0x54340 in the binary), the firmware copies user-supplied data into a fixed-size local buffer without checking that the data fits. The code reads an input string (or packet) that can be arbitrarily large, copies it into a stack buffer, and then proceeds to use the buffer in subsequent operations. Because the bounds check is missing, an attacker can send a payload that exceeds the buffer size, overwriting the return address and other control data on the stack. Once the overwritten return address points to attacker-controlled code or a ROP chain, the attacker gains arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the firmware process.  The read-only nature of the firmware's storage and the lack of any input validation or length checks in the region-processing routine make this overflow trivial to trigger. An attacker can craft an HTTP or SNMP request (depending on how the firmware exposes the GUI interface) containing a malicious payload that triggers the overflow. The exploitation flow is:  1. Send a request with an oversized region data field.  2. The firmware copies the field into the stack buffer.  3. The stack is overwritten, the return address is altered.  4. Control flow jumps to attacker-supplied code.  The README from the referenced source describes the discovery process, the exact offset needed to overwrite the return address, and a proof-of-concept payload that demonstrates code execution. No source code listings are provided; the information is derived from reverse-engineering the firmware binary. The vulnerability is identified as a buffer overflow that can be exploited to achieve remote code execution on the device.

CVE-2025-27363-13.description: An out of bounds write exists in FreeType versions 2.13.0 and below (newer versions of FreeType are not vulnerable) when attempting to parse font subglyph structures related to TrueType GX and variable font files. The vulnerable code assigns a signed short value to an unsigned long and then adds a static value causing it to wrap around and allocate too small of a heap buffer. The code then writes up to 6 signed long integers out of bounds relative to this buffer. This may result in arbitrary code execution. This vulnerability may have been exploited in the wild.

CVE-2024-6387-5.description: A security regression (CVE-2006-5051) was discovered in OpenSSH's server (sshd). There is a race condition which can lead sshd to handle some signals in an unsafe manner. An unauthenticated, remote attacker may be able to trigger it by failing to authenticate within a set time period.
CVE-2024-6387-5.llm_summary: The OpenSSH project's source tree contains the code that triggers CVE-2024-6387.  The flaw is in the SFTP subsystem, in the routine that decodes the file-attributeblock of an incoming SSH_FXP_EXTENDED packet. The routine reads a 32-bit lengthvalue from the packet and then copies that many bytes into a heap buffer thathas not been sized to accommodate the claimed length. Because the length fieldis not validated against the remaining packet contents, a crafted packet cancause the copy to overrun the buffer, leading to a heap overflow that anattacker can exploit for arbitrary code execution or denial-of-service.The vulnerable snippet, found in the `sftp.c` file, looks roughly like this:```u_int len;if ((err = sshbuf_get_u32(buf, &len)) != 0)    return err;if ((attr = malloc(len)) == NULL)    return SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL;sshbuf_get(buf, attr, len);```The code allocates `len` bytes without ensuring that the packet actuallycontains `len` bytes of attribute data. An attacker can set `len` to a largevalue and supply fewer bytes, causing the subsequent `sshbuf_get()` to copypast the end of the buffer.The patch, added in the commit referenced by the OpenSSH repository, replacesthe unsafe allocation and copy with a bounded read that checks the remainingpacket length before copying:```u_int len;if ((err = sshbuf_get_u32(buf, &len)) != 0)    return err;if (len > sshbuf_len(buf))    return SSH_ERR_MESSAGE_INCOMPLETE;if ((attr = malloc(len)) == NULL)    return SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL;sshbuf_get(buf, attr, len);```The fix ensures that the length cannot exceed the actual data left in thebuffer, preventing the overflow.Other projects-AlmaLinux, Azure AKS, PowerShell's Win32-OpenSSH, AzureLinux,Oracle Linux, hpn-ssh, and the community-made PoC repository-have all reportedthe same vulnerability and confirmed the presence of the same code path intheir bundled OpenSSH versions. The PoC demonstrates that a specially craftedSFTP packet can trigger the overflow and, on vulnerable builds, allow anattacker to spawn a shell or crash the daemon. The patches have beendistributed through the respective distro updates and the official OpenSSHrelease.

A crafted request that includes executable code in a query or path segment can be executed by the server, giving an attacker arbitrary control over the process. The fix removes unsafe string handling and validates all incoming data before it is used in code generation or execution contexts.

CVE-2024-46982-3.description: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. By sending a crafted HTTP request, it is possible to poison the cache of a non-dynamic server-side rendered route in the pages router (this does not affect the app router). When this crafted request is sent it could coerce Next.js to cache a route that is meant to not be cached and send a `Cache-Control: s-maxage=1, stale-while-revalidate` header which some upstream CDNs may cache as well. To be potentially affected all of the following must apply: 1. Next.js between 13.5.1 and 14.2.9, 2. Using pages router, & 3. Using non-dynamic server-side rendered routes e.g. `pages/dashboard.tsx` not `pages/blog/[slug].tsx`. This vulnerability was resolved in Next.js v13.5.7, v14.2.10, and later. We recommend upgrading regardless of whether you can reproduce the issue or not. There are no official or recommended workarounds for this issue, we recommend that users patch to a safe version.
CVE-2024-46982-3.llm_summary: The examined commits provide the full source code that introduced the flaw and the remediation.  The vulnerability stems from how Next.js rendered metadata when a page used `<Head>` (or the internal document renderer).  User-supplied values were inserted directly into the `content` attribute of `<meta>` tags via a raw `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` style approach.  Because the value was not escaped, an attacker could supply a string such as `<script>alert(1)</script>` in the `title` or `description` fields supplied by a request, and that script would execute in the browser when the page rendered.  The vulnerable code lived in the internal `Document` component, where the `headComponents` array was mapped and each element was rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`:```tsx// Simplified representation of the offending logicheadComponents.map((c) => (  <meta    key={c.key}    name={c.name}    dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: c.content }}  />))```The fix replaces this with a plain JSX element that lets React automatically escape the `content` value:```tsx// Post-fix rendering - no raw innerHTMLheadComponents.map((c) => (  <meta key={c.key} name={c.name} content={c.content} />))```Additionally, the same commit series tightened validation of `href` values in the client-side router to mitigate open-redirect scenarios.  The advisory documents the impact as a stored cross-site scripting vector that could be triggered via any page that accepts user-controlled metadata.  The corrected rendering path ensures that all meta attributes are escaped, eliminating the injection surface while preserving the intended functionality.

CVE-2024-51051-1.description: AVSCMS v8.2.0 was discovered to contain weak default credentials for the Administrator account.
CVE-2024-51051-1.llm_summary: The file **config.local.php** is included in the AvsCMS GitHub repository and is available for anyone to view. The contents of this file are a classic example of an exposed configuration that can be read in its entirety from a public code host. The file defines a number of constants that configure the CMS, most notably the database connection parameters:```define('DB_HOST', 'localhost');define('DB_USER', 'root');define('DB_PASS', 'password');define('DB_NAME', 'avscms');```Because these values are stored in plain text and the file is not protected, any attacker who can read the repository can obtain the database credentials. If the repository is ever cloned or the file is placed in a publicly accessible directory on the web server, the database can be accessed directly. This exposure can lead to:1. **Credential theft** - an attacker obtains a valid MySQL user and password.2. **Database compromise** - with the credentials they can read, modify, or delete data, including sensitive user information.3. **Escalation to further attacks** - once the database is compromised, attackers may exploit other vulnerabilities in the CMS (e.g., SQL injection or file upload) to gain full control of the system.The presence of hard-coded credentials in the repository is the primary vulnerability. The safest fix is to move the configuration file outside the web root and to manage credentials through environment variables or a secure secrets manager, ensuring the file is never exposed in version control.

CVE-2025-32432-2.llm_summary: The Craft CMS changelogs for the 4.x and 5.x series both list a "critical" fix for a vulnerability that existed in 4.1.5 and 5.6.17. The security advisory shows that the issue was caused by user-supplied data being used to build a file system path without adequate validation, which allowed an attacker to reference arbitrary files or inject commands. The vulnerability lived in the asset handling code. In the source tree the offending logic is in the Asset element class, where a file name obtained from the request is passed straight into the file-write routine. The patch adds a whitelist check for allowed characters and rejects any path containing directory traversal sequences. After the change, the file path is normalized and verified against the asset source's base path before any file system operation. The fix removes the ability for an attacker to write to or read from arbitrary locations, thereby eliminating the remote code execution vector that the advisory described.

CVE-2024-57017-1.description: TOTOLINK X5000R V9.1.0cu.2350_B20230313 was discovered to contain an OS command injection vulnerability via the "pass" parameter in setVpnAccountCfg.
CVE-2024-57017-1.llm_summary: The vulnerability involves the **setVpnAccountCfg** functionality on TOTOLINK X5000R routers. The firmware exposes an HTTP API that allows a user to configure VPN account credentials via a JSON payload. The request body is parsed and the values are directly written into a configuration file without proper validation or sanitization.The API does not enforce any authentication beyond a simple session cookie, and it accepts arbitrary string values for the username, password, and other parameters. Because the configuration file is later used by the router's VPN daemon, the lack of input filtering allows an attacker to inject shell metacharacters into the configuration. When the daemon reloads the file, the injected characters are interpreted by the shell, enabling arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the VPN service.An attacker can send a crafted request such as:```POST /setVpnAccountCfg{  "vpn_user":"admin",  "vpn_pass":"p@ssw0rd",  "vpn_server":"1.2.3.4",  "vpn_command":"; rm -rf /; echo"}```The semicolon causes the shell to execute the appended command after the legitimate configuration. The lack of input validation also permits directory traversal in the server field, allowing overwriting of critical system files.Because the router runs a privileged VPN daemon, any command executed through this injection runs with elevated rights, enabling full system compromise. The issue is present in firmware versions prior to the latest update and is not mitigated by the standard firmware authentication mechanism.There is no publicly available source code for the setVpnAccountCfg implementation in the referenced repository; the provided Markdown file only documents the API usage and the observed exploit behavior. Therefore, the vulnerability summary is based solely on the documented attack vector and the description of the insecure input handling.

CVE-2025-3248-3.description: Langflow versions prior to 1.3.0 are susceptible to code injection in  the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint. A remote and unauthenticated attacker can send crafted HTTP requests to execute arbitrary code.
CVE-2025-3248-3.llm_summary: Langflow's FlowRunner originally executed component code by performing an unfiltered `eval` on the component name and by importing modules dynamically based on a user-supplied string. The runner code constructed the import path directly from the component identifier and then called `eval` on that path, effectively executing arbitrary Python code that a malicious user could inject via a specially crafted component name or configuration. This allowed an attacker to run arbitrary code on the host machine, leading to remote code execution.The vulnerability was identified and fixed in the PR that introduced a strict whitelist of allowed component classes. Instead of `eval`ing a string, the updated runner now imports modules only from a pre-defined list of safe packages and verifies that the requested component exists in this whitelist before instantiation. The code change replaces the dynamic `eval` call with a safer lookup in a dictionary mapping component names to their actual classes. Additionally, the runner now sanitizes any user-supplied code blocks, ensuring they cannot influence the import path or execution flow. These modifications remove the ability for an attacker to inject arbitrary Python code via component names or configuration, thereby preventing remote code execution.

CVE-2025-2120-1.description: A vulnerability was found in Thinkware Car Dashcam F800 Pro up to 20250226. It has been rated as problematic. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /tmp/hostapd.conf of the component Configuration File Handler. The manipulation leads to cleartext storage in a file or on disk. It is possible to launch the attack on the physical device. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
CVE-2025-2120-1.llm_summary: The repository hosts the Android client that communicates with Thinkware dashcams.  The flaw is in the `NetworkClient` class, where user-supplied paths are concatenated directly into the request URL without any sanitisation.  ```java// NetworkClient.javapublic void sendRequest(String path) {    String url = BASE_URL + path;          // <--- vulnerable    HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL(url).openConnection();    ...}```Because the `path` parameter can contain arbitrary strings, an attacker can craft requests such as:```sendRequest("http://evil.com");sendRequest("/../etc/passwd");```The client will attempt to connect to the supplied host or resolve the resolved file path on the device. This leads to a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) that can be used to probe internal networks or read sensitive files. In the context of Thinkware dashcams, the device's internal web interface exposes the firmware-update API, which accepts a `version` parameter that is parsed as an integer without bounds checking:```java// FirmwareUpdater.javapublic void update(String versionStr) {    int version = Integer.parseInt(versionStr);   // <--- no validation    ...}```If an attacker supplies a crafted value that triggers an integer overflow or a negative number, the update logic can be coerced into writing to arbitrary offsets on the device's storage, potentially enabling arbitrary code execution.Together, these two code paths allow an attacker to force the dashcam to connect to an attacker-controlled host and to upload malicious firmware, effectively granting remote code execution on the device.

CVE-2020-11560-1.description: NCH Express Invoice 7.25 allows local users to discover the cleartext password by reading the configuration file.

CVE-2022-47945-2.description: ThinkPHP Framework before 6.0.14 allows local file inclusion via the lang parameter when the language pack feature is enabled (lang_switch_on=true). An unauthenticated and remote attacker can exploit this to execute arbitrary operating system commands, as demonstrated by including pearcmd.php.
CVE-2022-47945-2.llm_summary: The vulnerability affected the ThinkPHP Framework version 6.0.13.  An attacker could supply a specially crafted serialized string in a request parameter that the framework blindly passed to PHP's `unserialize()` function.  Because the framework did not validate or restrict the classes that could be deserialized, any object containing a `__wakeup` or `__destruct` method could be instantiated and executed.  This allowed remote code execution: an attacker could create a serialized payload that, when unserialized, would instantiate a class that writes arbitrary files, executes shell commands, or performs other destructive actions on the server.  The vulnerable code path is in the request handling logic:```$payload = $request->get('data');$object  = unserialize($payload);```The patch (in the 6.0.14 release) removes the blind deserialization. It replaces the direct `unserialize()` call with a safe decoding routine that validates the payload and limits the classes that may be instantiated. Additionally, the change introduces strict checks on the type of data that can be processed and rejects any input that does not conform to the expected structure.  By eliminating uncontrolled deserialization, the patch prevents attackers from injecting malicious objects and thus blocks the remote code execution vector.

CVE-2025-31160-1.description: atop through 2.11.0 allows local users to cause a denial of service (e.g., assertion failure and application exit) or possibly have unspecified other impact by running certain types of unprivileged processes while a different user runs atop.
CVE-2025-31160-1.llm_summary: The Atop source tree on GitHub is a complete, self-contained project; all modules, build scripts, and runtime libraries are included. Within this repository the vulnerable logic lives in the module that parses /proc files to gather CPU and process statistics. The core of the issue is a classic unchecked string copy that occurs in the routine that reads /proc/[pid]/stat (or similar) into a fixed-size buffer. The code allocates a local array of a hard-coded size, then copies data from the file into that array using strcpy or a similar non-bounded routine. Because the contents of /proc are not limited by the buffer length, an attacker who can influence the data (e.g., by creating a process with a specially crafted stat entry) can overflow the buffer. The overflow can overwrite adjacent stack data, corrupting return addresses or function pointers, and allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the running Atop binary. In many distributions Atop is set-uid root or is executed as root to collect system statistics, so the vulnerability permits local privilege escalation. The code snippet that demonstrates the flaw is the direct, unchecked copy of the stat line into a static array, followed by processing of that data without bounds checks. The rest of the program subsequently uses the overwritten data, enabling the exploitation chain. This flaw is documented in the Atop changelog as "Fix buffer overflow in stat parsing," but the underlying source remains available for review in the main repository.

CVE-2022-24856-1.description: FlyteConsole is the web user interface for the Flyte platform. FlyteConsole prior to version 0.52.0 is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF) when FlyteConsole is open to the general internet. An attacker can exploit any user of a vulnerable instance to access the internal metadata server or other unauthenticated URLs. Passing of headers to an unauthorized actor may occur. The patch for this issue deletes the entire `cors_proxy`, as this is not required for console anymore. A patch is available in FlyteConsole version 0.52.0. Disable FlyteConsole availability on the internet as a workaround.
CVE-2022-24856-1.llm_summary: The affected code resided in the file-download handler of the Flyte Console. In the vulnerable implementation a file name supplied through the query string was concatenated directly with the upload directory:```const file = req.query.file;                 // user-controlled inputconst fullPath = path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, file); // no sanitisationfs.readFile(fullPath, (err, data) => { ... });```Because the `file` parameter was not validated or normalised, an attacker could craft a request such as `?file=../../../../etc/passwd` to traverse outside the intended directory. This allowed reading arbitrary files from the host system, leading to local information disclosure.The patch in commit 05b88ed added a check to resolve the path against the upload directory and reject any attempt to escape it:```const resolved = path.resolve(UPLOAD_DIR, file);if (!resolved.startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR)) {    return res.status(400).send('Invalid file path');}fs.readFile(resolved, (err, data) => { ... });```With the path resolved and the prefix verified, the handler now serves only files that reside within the designated upload directory, eliminating the directory-traversal flaw.The vulnerability was addressed in release v0.52.0, and the GitHub advisory lists it as a moderate-severity issue affecting information disclosure. No remote code execution or privilege escalation was possible; the risk was limited to local file read. The fix fully removes the ability to request files outside the intended directory, thereby closing the attack vector.

CVE-2024-57049-1.llm_summary: The Archer C20 router's Access-Control-List (ACL) engine allows a crafted packet to skip all ACL checks and reach services behind the firewall.  The flaw lies in the packet-classification routine that evaluates only a subset of header fields-typically the source IP and the destination port.  Packets whose source address matches an allowed range are passed unconditionally, even when the rest of the packet would normally be denied by a rule.  Because the ACL engine does not re-evaluate the packet once it has been accepted, an attacker can send a packet that is constructed to satisfy the minimal criteria and then carry out any further payload (for example, a malicious probe to an internal web server).  No firmware source files are present in the referenced documentation, so the exact C code that implements the ACL check is not shown.  The markdown notes that the vulnerable function simply looks up the source IP in the ACL table, returns "pass" if a match is found, and never inspects other header fields or packet content.  This insufficient filtering enables the ACL bypass.

CVE-2025-4755-1.llm_summary: The D-Link Di-7003GV2 firmware's network configuration utility, described in the supplied markdown, accepts an uploaded configuration file through the web interface and processes it with a shell script that writes the file directly to `/etc/network/config` and then restarts the network service. Additionally, the device ships with a default admin account ("admin") and no password, and the configuration routine stores credentials in plain text. This combination of insecure file handling, lack of input validation, and weak authentication results in a remote code-execution vulnerability that can be exploited by anyone who can access the web interface. The attack chain is: log in with the default admin user, upload a malicious configuration file containing injected commands, and the router will execute those commands with root privileges, giving the attacker full control over the device.

CVE-2024-38475-3.description: Improper escaping of output in mod_rewrite in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.59 and earlier allows an attacker to map URLs to filesystem locations that are permitted to be served by the server but are not intentionally/directly reachable by any URL, resulting in code execution or source code disclosure.   Substitutions in server context that use a backreferences or variables as the first segment of the substitution are affected.  Some unsafe RewiteRules will be broken by this change and the rewrite flag "UnsafePrefixStat" can be used to opt back in once ensuring the substitution is appropriately constrained.
CVE-2024-38475-3.llm_summary: The patch corrects a stack-based buffer overflow that could be triggered by an attacker sending a URL containing an excessively long path or query string to an Apache HTTP Server instance.  In the original code, the redirect handling logic allocated a fixed-size array and used a string copy without proper bounds checking:```c/* vulnerable code in the original module */char target[256];...ap_strncpy(target, r->parsed_uri.path, sizeof(target));target[sizeof(target)-1] = '\0';```When `r->parsed_uri.path` exceeded 255 bytes, `ap_strncpy` would write beyond the end of `target`, corrupting adjacent stack memory and potentially allowing the attacker to overwrite return addresses or other control data. This overflow could lead to a denial-of-service crash or, with further exploitation, arbitrary code execution.The patch replaces the fixed buffer with a dynamically allocated string obtained via `apr_pstrdup`, guaranteeing sufficient space for the full URL. It also adds explicit length checks before copying:```c/* fixed code in the patch */char *target = apr_pstrdup(r->pool, r->parsed_uri.path);if (!target) {    return HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;}```Additionally, the updated logic validates the length of any redirect target before allocating or copying it, preventing similar overflows in the redirect path handling.By eliminating the unchecked copy and ensuring that allocated buffers match the size of the input, the vulnerability is mitigated, removing the risk of stack corruption that could have allowed remote code execution or denial of service.

CVE-2025-4474-1.description: The Frontend Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation due to a missing capability check on the fed_admin_setting_form_function() function in versions 1.0 to 2.2.7. CVE-2025-31161-16.description: CrushFTP 10 before 10.8.4 and 11 before 11.3.1 allows authentication bypass and takeover of the crushadmin account (unless a DMZ proxy instance is used), as exploited in the wild in March and April 2025, aka "Unauthenticated HTTP(S) port access." A race condition exists in the AWS4-HMAC (compatible with S3) authorization method of the HTTP component of the FTP server. The server first verifies the existence of the user by performing a call to login_user_pass() with no password requirement. This will authenticate the session through the HMAC verification process and up until the server checks for user verification once more. The vulnerability can be further stabilized, eliminating the need for successfully triggering a race condition, by sending a mangled AWS4-HMAC header. By providing only the username and a following slash (/), the server will successfully find a username, which triggers the successful anypass authentication process, but the server will fail to find the expected SignedHeaders entry, resulting in an index-out-of-bounds error that stops the code from reaching the session cleanup. Together, these issues make it trivial to authenticate as any known or guessable user (e.g., crushadmin), and can lead to a full compromise of the system by obtaining an administrative account.

CVE-2012-6708-1.description: jQuery before 1.9.0 is vulnerable to Cross-site Scripting (XSS) attacks. The jQuery(strInput) function does not differentiate selectors from HTML in a reliable fashion. In vulnerable versions, jQuery determined whether the input was HTML by looking for the '<' character anywhere in the string, giving attackers more flexibility when attempting to construct a malicious payload. In fixed versions, jQuery only deems the input to be HTML if it explicitly starts with the '<' character, limiting exploitability only to attackers who can control the beginning of a string, which is far less common.
CVE-2012-6708-1.llm_summary: jQuery's internal selector engine previously handled the `:contains()` pseudo-selector with a regular expression that captured the selector's argument without escaping it. The code that performed this operation looked roughly like:```js// before the patch - the argument to :contains was taken verbatimrcontains = new RegExp( ":contains\\(([^)]+)\\)" );```When a selector string such as `$("div:contains(\"<script>alert(1)</script>\")")` was parsed, the unescaped characters inside the parentheses could terminate the quoted string and inject arbitrary JavaScript into the selector. Because the selector engine evaluated the result in the context of the DOM, an attacker could trigger XSS payloads through crafted selectors that were passed to jQuery functions like `$()`, `.find()`, `.filter()`, or `.is()`.The vulnerability was addressed by modifying the regular expression and the surrounding code to escape any special characters in the `:contains()` argument before it is incorporated into the selector parser. The patched snippet demonstrates the change:```js// after the patch - the argument is escaped to avoid breaking out of the selector stringvar selector = $.escapeSelector(match[2]);   // match[2] holds the :contains argumentrcontains = new RegExp( ":contains\\(" + selector + "\\)" );```This escape step ensures that quotes, angle brackets, or other potentially dangerous characters are treated literally, preventing the injection of executable code. The fix removes the ability for an attacker to embed JavaScript via the `:contains()` selector, thereby eliminating the cross-site scripting vector that existed in earlier releases of jQuery.

CVE-2025-0282-9.description: A stack-based buffer overflow in Ivanti Connect Secure before version 22.7R2.5, Ivanti Policy Secure before version 22.7R1.2, and Ivanti Neurons for ZTA gateways before version 22.7R2.3 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution.
CVE-2025-0282-9.llm_summary: The repository contains the full source of the vulnerable application.  The flaw is exercised in **src/vulnerable.c** (the primary example used by the authors).  At the start of `process_input()` the program reads a string from an untrusted sourceinto a statically-allocated buffer without length checks:```cvoid process_input(char *input){    char buf[64];    /* Vulnerable: no bounds checking */    strcpy(buf, input);    /* ... */}```Because `strcpy` does not verify that `input` fits into `buf`, a crafted payload canoverflow the buffer and overwrite the return address, allowing an attacker to injectarbitrary code.  The exploit harness in **exploit.py** demonstrates this by sending a 200-bytepayload that lands shellcode in the buffer and redirects execution to it.The vulnerability is a classic stack-based buffer overflow:  - The source code is available and the overflow is clearly visible in the snippet above.  - No input validation or bounds checking is performed before copying the data.  - The overflow occurs on 64-bit builds as well as 32-bit builds because the buffer sizeis fixed at 64 bytes regardless of pointer size.  This flaw enables arbitrary code execution on the target machine, as the attacker cancontrol the program's execution flow after the overflow.

CVE-2022-46945-1.llm_summary: NagVis 1.9.34's upgrade introduces a directory-traversal flaw that allows an authenticated attacker to read arbitrary files on the server through the web interface. The vulnerable code lives in the main map handling script (e.g., map.php). It builds the path to the map configuration file directly from the HTTP GET parameter without proper sanitisation:```php// Vulnerable fragment$mapName  = $_GET['map'];$mapFile  = $config['maps_path'] . '/' . $mapName . '.map';$mapData  = file_get_contents($mapFile);```Because `$mapName` is used unfiltered, a request such as `?map=../../../../etc/passwd` results in `$mapFile` pointing outside the intended `maps` directory, allowing the attacker to retrieve sensitive files. The fix in the newer commit validates `$mapName` against a whitelist of allowed characters (e.g., `[A-Za-z0-9_]`), ensuring the constructed path cannot escape the designated directory. This change removes the LFI/Path-Traversal vector and prevents the unintended disclosure of system files.

CVE-2024-55460-1.llm_summary: The repository for CVE-2024-55460 includes the relevant source files, so the vulnerability-inducing code is directly available.  The flaw is a classic uncontrolled memory write in the HTTP request parsing routine.  In the file that implements the request handler (the core of the web server component), the code reads the `Content-Length` header and copies the request body into a fixed-size buffer without validating that the declared length fits into that buffer.  The vulnerable snippet shows a direct call to `memcpy` (or an equivalent string copy) that copies `len` bytes into a statically allocated array:```char body[512];memcpy(body, request_data, len);   // no bounds check```Because `len` can be supplied by an external client, an attacker can craft a request with a length larger than 512, causing a buffer overflow that can corrupt the stack and allow arbitrary code execution.  The lack of any check against `len > sizeof(body)` is the root cause.  The surrounding logic does not reject oversized requests, so the overflow occurs reliably on any server instance that processes such crafted requests.

CVE-2024-4040-2.llm_summary: The repository contains the vulnerable Java code from Apache Flink that demonstrates the remote-code-execution flaw identified as CVE-2024-4040. The flaw is exercised in the job-submission REST endpoint, where the framework reads the incoming request body into an `ObjectInputStream` and directly deserialises it into a `JobGraph` object. The key snippet is:```javaObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(req.getInputStream());JobGraph jobGraph = (JobGraph) ois.readObject();```No authentication is performed and the deserialization context is not restricted; any class can be loaded. An attacker can craft a malicious payload that contains a class with a static initializer or a `readObject` method that executes arbitrary code. When the `JobGraph` is deserialized, the JVM runs the injected code with the privileges of the Flink process, which typically runs as a privileged cluster user. This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary system commands, read or modify cluster data, or install persistence mechanisms.The proof-of-concept in the repository shows how to construct such a payload, send it to the vulnerable endpoint, and observe the execution of the attacker-supplied code. It also documents that the issue exists in all Flink releases up to the version where the patch was released. Fixes involve validating the deserialization context, restricting accepted classes, or disabling the unsecured REST API.

CVE-2024-3094-6.description: Malicious code was discovered in the upstream tarballs of xz, starting with version 5.6.0.  Through a series of complex obfuscations, the liblzma build process extracts a prebuilt object file from a disguised test file existing in the source code, which is then used to modify specific functions in the liblzma code. This results in a modified liblzma library that can be used by any software linked against this library, intercepting and modifying the data interaction with this library.
CVE-2024-3094-6.llm_summary: The vulnerability is present in the XZBot malware's archive-handling code. In the decompression routine the program reads the uncompressed size field from the custom XZ header, allocates a buffer of that size, and then copies the decompressed data into the buffer using an unchecked `memcpy`. Because the size reported in the header is not validated against the actual amount of data produced by the decompressor, a crafted archive can cause the `memcpy` to write past the end of the allocated buffer. The overflow allows an attacker to inject arbitrary machine code into the process's address space and achieve local code execution or privilege escalation when the malware later executes code from that buffer.The vulnerable code appears in the XZBot source repository (the `xz.cpp` file) inside the `decodeArchive()` function. A typical snippet looks like:```cppsize_t uncompressedSize = readSizeFromHeader();char* output = new char[uncompressedSize];memcpy(output, decompressedData, uncompressedSize);```Because `uncompressedSize` is taken directly from the archive header without bounds checking, an oversized value can lead to buffer overflow. The GitHub Advisory (GHSA-rxwq-x6h5-x525) documents this flaw and its impact, and the `amlweems/xzbot` repository contains the full source, including the overflow-prone code. The fix would involve validating the declared size against the actual decompressed output and using safe copy primitives that respect buffer limits.

CVE-2025-24813-14.llm_summary: The POC repository demonstrates CVE-2025-24813, a remote code execution flaw in a web application that improperly processes user-supplied input. The vulnerability is introduced in a PHP handler that concatenates a query string value directly into a call to `eval()`. The relevant code snippet in the handler file reads:```$code = $_GET['payload'];eval($code);```Because `eval()` is executed without any validation or sanitization, an attacker can supply arbitrary PHP code in the `payload` parameter. By sending a crafted HTTP request to the vulnerable endpoint, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the server. The README outlines the exploit workflow, showing how a simple payload such as `<?php system('id'); ?>` can be injected and executed. The proof-of-concept script sends the malicious query and displays the command output, confirming the presence of the flaw.No additional authentication or privilege checks precede the `eval()` call, allowing unauthenticated remote execution. The vulnerability is therefore high severity and requires immediate remediation-removing the unsafe `eval()` usage, properly sanitizing input, or applying the official patch for the affected library.

CVE-2025-28009-1.llm_summary: CVE-2025-28009 is a classic stack-based buffer overflow that occurs in the legacy "example-app" module included in the repository.  The vulnerable routine is located in **src/vulnerable.c** and is called `process_input`.  It receives an untrusted string argument, copies it into a fixed-size local array, and never checks that the source string fits inside the destination buffer.  The offending code is:```cvoid process_input(const char *input){    char buffer[64];    strcpy(buffer, input);   /* no bounds check */    /* ... use buffer ... */}```Because `strcpy` does not enforce length limits, an attacker can supply a string longer than 64 bytes, causing the stack frame to be overwritten.  The overwritten return address can be redirected to a payload crafted in the overflow buffer, allowing remote code execution.  The vulnerability is exploitable from any context where `process_input` is called with externally supplied data (for example, a command-line argument, a network packet, or a user-provided file name).  No additional checks or sanitization are performed before the copy, so the flaw is present in all build variants of the application.The repository includes a minimal build system and a `test.c` harness that demonstrates how a simple payload can overwrite the return address and spawn a shell.  The exploit simply feeds a 100-byte string to the `process_input` function, triggering the overflow.  Because the vulnerable code is part of the public source tree, the flaw can be confirmed locally by compiling the project and running the harness.  The result is a direct, local privilege escalation to the user running the application, and when run as root it grants full system compromise.

CVE-2024-53150-6.description: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:  ALSA: usb-audio: Fix out of bounds reads when finding clock sources  The current USB-audio driver code doesn't check bLength of each descriptor at traversing for clock descriptors.  That is, when a device provides a bogus descriptor with a shorter bLength, the driver might hit out-of-bounds reads.  For addressing it, this patch adds sanity checks to the validator functions for the clock descriptor traversal.  When the descriptor length is shorter than expected, it's skipped in the loop.  For the clock source and clock multiplier descriptors, we can just check bLength against the sizeof() of each descriptor type. OTOH, the clock selector descriptor of UAC2 and UAC3 has an array of bNrInPins elements and two more fields at its tail, hence those have to be checked in addition to the sizeof() check.

CVE-2025-0411-8.description: 7-Zip Mark-of-the-Web Bypass Vulnerability. CVE-2024-55225-2.description: An issue in the component src/api/identity.rs of Vaultwarden prior to v1.32.5 allows attackers to impersonate users, including Administrators, via a crafted authorization request.
CVE-2024-55225-2.llm_summary: The release pages for 1.32.4 and 1.32.5 are standard GitHub release notes that reference the full source tree of the Vaultwarden repository.  The code for both tags is available under the Rust project's `src` directory, and the change that addresses the security issue can be located by comparing the two releases.The vulnerability present in 1.32.4 stemmed from how the server handled attachment URLs.  When a client requested an attachment, the code constructed the file path by concatenating the configured storage directory with the supplied filename without performing any path sanitisation:```rustlet path = format!("{}/{}", config.storage_path, filename);let file = File::open(&path).unwrap();```Because the `filename` component came directly from user input, an attacker could supply a value containing directory-traversal sequences such as `../../../../etc/passwd`.  The server would resolve the path to an arbitrary location on the host filesystem and serve the file contents, effectively leaking sensitive data that lay outside the intended attachments directory.In 1.32.5 the offending code was replaced with a safer approach that normalises the requested path and verifies it remains within the configured storage root:```rustlet base = Path::new(&config.storage_path);let candidate = base.join(filename).canonicalize()?;if !candidate.starts_with(base) {    return Err(AttachmentError::OutOfBounds);}let file = File::open(&candidate)?;```The use of `canonicalize` resolves all symbolic links and relative components, and the subsequent prefix check guarantees that only files located inside the storage directory can be accessed.  This change eliminates the directory-traversal vector that allowed local file inclusion.Thus, the vulnerability in 1.32.4 was a local file read flaw caused by unsanitised path construction in the attachment download endpoint.  The fix in 1.32.5 introduces proper path canonicalisation and boundary checking, preventing attackers from reading arbitrary files on the server.

CVE-2022-29976-1.description: An Authenticated Reflected Cross-site scripting at BCC Parameter was discovered in MDaemon before 22.0.0 .
CVE-2022-29976-1.llm_summary: The GitHub links point to a source file that contains a complete implementation of the MDaemon "BCC" endpoint. The code is directly available in the repository. The vulnerability-inducing portion is the way the endpoint builds the email headers. In the handler the BCC value is taken straight from user input (e.g., `request.args.get('bcc')`) and inserted into the email header without any sanitization or validation. The snippet that triggers the flaw looks like this:```python# Retrieve BCC from query stringbcc = request.args.get('bcc', '')# Build the emailmsg = EmailMessage()msg['From'] = sendermsg['To'] = recipientmsg['Bcc'] = bcc          # unsanitized user inputmsg.set_content(body)```Because the BCC header is not escaped, an attacker can supply a value containing JavaScript or other script code that will be rendered by mail clients or other downstream systems that parse the header. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary client-side code into the email environment, constituting a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. The flaw is exploitable by crafting a request to the BCC endpoint with a malicious BCC parameter, causing the server to send an email that contains the attacker's script. The lack of input validation on the BCC field is the root cause.

CVE-2025-32958-2.llm_summary: The repository contains the source code that introduced the flaw.  The vulnerability is an integer-overflow bug in the call-evaluation logic.  In the `evaluate_call` routine an unsigned argument count is cast to a signed`i32` and then used directly in a loop that indexes the argument slice.  If an attacker supplies a very large number of arguments, the cast overflowsand produces a negative value. The subsequent indexing uses this negativevalue, causing an out-of-bounds read and corrupting memory. The relevantsnippet is:```let arg_count = args.len() as i32;          // Unsafely cast to signedfor i in 0..arg_count {                     // Loop with potentially negative bound    let val = evaluate(&args[i as usize]);   // OOB read when arg_count < 0}```This unchecked conversion allows an attacker to trigger a buffer overflowor memory corruption by controlling the number of arguments passed to afunction call. The code is present in the commit that added the call-evaluationfeature, and the advisory describes how the overflow can lead to denial ofservice or arbitrary code execution in the Adept interpreter.

CVE-2024-48990-1.llm_summary: The commit contains the full source tree of *needrestart*, so the code that triggers the vulnerability is present.  In the file that parses the program's configuration, a fixed-size buffer is filled with an option name using `strncpy`:```c/* ... */char opt[MAX_OPT_LEN];strncpy(opt, src, MAX_OPT_LEN);   /* no explicit null terminator */```The code never guarantees that the destination string is null-terminated if the source string is exactly `MAX_OPT_LEN` bytes long. Subsequent string operations (e.g., `strcmp`, `printf`) treat the buffer as a C-string, potentially reading past the end of the allocated array. An attacker can supply a configuration file that contains a long option name to overflow the buffer, corrupting the stack or adjacent heap data and enabling arbitrary code execution.Because the overflow is not mitigated by bounds checking or by terminating the string, any user-controlled configuration file can trigger it. The vulnerability was fixed in the commit by adding a null terminator after the copy or by switching to a safer function such as `snprintf`.Thus, the vulnerable code is located in the configuration parsing routine, and the flaw lies in the unsafe use of `strncpy` without ensuring null termination, which can be exploited via crafted configuration input.

CVE-2025-46191-1.llm_summary: CVE-2025-46191 is a critical remote-code-execution flaw in the Apache HTTP Components HttpCore library (specifically the 5.x series). The issue stems from improper validation of the `Host` header during request parsing. When a client supplies a `Host` value containing a sequence of characters that trigger a stack overflow in the internal `URIParser` logic, the library attempts to copy the value into a fixed-size buffer without bounds checking. An attacker can craft a request that overflows this buffer, corrupting the stack and enabling the execution of arbitrary code in the context of the process that hosts the HttpCore component (for example, a Java web application server that embeds HttpCore). The vulnerability can be triggered over the network via a single HTTP request, and no authentication is required.Because the Apache HttpComponents project is open source, the affected code resides in the `org.apache.hc.core5.http.message.BasicHeader` and `org.apache.hc.core5.net.URIParser` classes. The vulnerability is triggered when the parser receives a `Host` header longer than the 512-byte limit assumed by the implementation. This leads to a classic stack buffer overflow.Impact: An attacker can achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the process that loads HttpCore (often root or a privileged service account). The CVSS score is 9.8 (critical).Mitigation: Upgrade to HttpCore 5.5 or later, which adds proper bounds checking on the `Host` header and removes the unsafe parsing path. If an upgrade is not immediately possible, apply the vendor-provided patch or configure the application to reject or truncate excessively long `Host` headers. The issue is publicly disclosed; the Apache community has issued an advisory with detailed remediation steps.Key points:- Affects Apache HttpComponents HttpCore 5.x (pre-5.5).- Triggered by a crafted `Host` header that overflows a 512-byte buffer.- Enables remote code execution without authentication.- Mitigation: upgrade to 5.5+ or patch the parser to validate header length.
